scope: Read-only inspection of live SQL query receipts, isolated browser/HTTP regression tests, and reload of only the supervised stateless public transport. No live business commands, compiler checks or provider calls were submitted.
diagnosis: The browser deadline enclosed queue wait plus execution. All seven delayed requests completed successfully after 12–58 seconds, but the browser had timed out and queued new refreshes. Parallel status/manifest refresh triggers amplified the serialized query-lane backlog.

fix.admission: Inventory and status clients request immediate SQL receipts with Prefer: respond-async. Legacy synchronous clients remain supported.
fix.observation: Each HTTP exchange is bounded to ten seconds; the original accepted receipt is observed for up to fifteen minutes. Transient receipt failures are retried without another query submission.
fix.coalescing: Each project/surface/generation shares one in-flight read. Repeated triggers retain at most one deferred follow-up. Source changes invalidate older responses; forced archive requests still await a forced snapshot.
fix.presentation: Pending inventory reads have an explicit neutral queued-refresh notice. Cached personal approval stays disabled while the current inventory is unconfirmed. Actual connection failures retain the previous error/backoff behavior.
fix.boundary: No direct worker/workspace/LSP access was introduced; all intake and receipt reads remain through the database API. The transport dispatch digest was reviewed and updated.

validation.receipt_deadline_case: A simulated 59-second query survives HTTP 503/408 receipt failures and follows the same command ID.
validation.browser_queued_refresh: An 11.5-second accepted query survives the former ten-second deadline. Ten repeated clicks and ten push notifications create one pending inventory submission; source text selection/tree DOM are preserved.
validation.visual_check: Narrow-pane queued-refresh notice reviewed; text and controls fit the existing pane.
